# `kernel/SubsurfaceManager.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/SubsurfaceManager.js`

SubsurfaceManager.js — kernel navigation service for app SUBSURFACES. A "surface" is an app's top-level display mode (window / overlay / tray — see manifest.surface). A "subsurface" is a navigable sub-location *inside* an app (a tab, section, or view), declared in the manifest as: "subsurfaces": [ { "id": "mixer", "label": "Volume Mixer", "icon": "🎚", "keywords": ["volume"] }, ... ] This service is the OS-level registry/tracker for deep-linking into those: - Active tracking: which subsurface each running app currently shows. - Pending nav:     a deep-link target stashed for an app that is still launching (the app reads it on mount via ui.pendingNavigate). - Recents + Pins:  persisted deep-link shortcuts (the "small UI shortcuts"), surfaced in the command palette / Start Menu. NOTE: This is distinct from SurfaceManager.js, which allocates WebGPU canvases. Events emitted on kernel.events: ui:navigate-subsurface  { appId, subsurfaceId, args }  — a deep-link was requested ui:subsurface-change    { appId, subsurfaceId }         — an app reported its active sub os:deeplinks-change     {}                              — pins/recents changed

## Functions

### `canonicalMediaAppId(appId)`

The retired Watch Party launch name addresses the combined player owner.

### `processCanReceiveUiDelivery(entry)`

True only after a registered process can synchronously receive UI delivery.

### `routeSubsurfaceNavigation(kernel, target, { manifest = null, openEvent = 'ui:open-panel', } = {})`

Route one deep link without racing an app's mount listener. Non-ready targets retain only the newest request and consume it after their listener binds.

### `flushPendingSubsurfaceNavigation(kernel, appId)`

Deliver a target that arrived after the app's early pending read but before ready.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```
